question: What did webpack 4.44.2 actually do with module bytes that are not valid UTF-8?
method: The holdout baseline lane is a webpack 4.44.2 create-react-app 4.0.3 production build that compiled green. Its emitted chunk is read back byte by byte and compared against the module bytes that went in.

The dependency under measurement ships two sibling files carrying the same Italian given names: one stored in ISO-8859-1, which is the module the holdout stopped on, and one stored in valid UTF-8. The second is the control. It fixes what the toolchain does to those same characters when the bytes are well formed, so the ISO-8859-1 result cannot be explained by anything downstream of the decode.
No adapter and no capability took part in producing this build. It is the baseline lane exactly as the holdout recorded it, and the migrated lane is not touched.

verdict.statement: webpack 4 decoded module bytes as UTF-8 and substituted U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER for every byte sequence UTF-8 cannot represent. That is the decoder loader-runner calls, Buffer.prototype.toString("utf-8"), which never throws, followed by a leading byte order mark strip.
verdict.refutedHypothesis: ISO-8859-1 decoding. The control module refutes it: the same six names, stored as well formed UTF-8 in the sibling file, reached the same chunk with their accents intact, while the ISO-8859-1 file reached it with U+FFFD in their place. A latin1 decode of the offending module would have produced the accented forms for that module too, and it did not.
verdict.consequence: Reproducing webpack means reproducing the loss. The production bundle this migration replaces shipped the replacement characters, so a decode that recovered the accents would be a behaviour change rather than parity.

nonclaims: No claim that the decoded text is correct Italian. It is not; the accents are gone. The claim is that it is what webpack 4 produced.
No claim about application source. The capability is scoped to the dependency closure, and invalid bytes in first-party source stay a build failure.
No claim about UTF-16 or UTF-32 module sources. Those are refused by name rather than decoded, which is narrower than webpack, and the refusal says so.
No claim about byte order marks on their own. A UTF-8 file carrying a BOM is valid UTF-8 and never reaches this capability.
No claim about stylesheets, JSON, or binary assets. Only JavaScript module sources are decoded.
No claim that the holdout was re-run. This reads the committed baseline artefacts of the run that already happened; the migrated lane is untouched and its FAIL receipt stands.
No claim that this capability makes the holdout green. The migrated lane stopped at the first unloadable module, so every demand behind that point remains unobserved.

freezeOrder.statement: This capability postdates the tranche-one adapter freeze. The holdout that named it was measured under composite fingerprint d9f75ef677cb850f664cc188abf77b8ebfd24e84cb58d147b74e9bbaa143eb77 with zero adapter bytes changed. That freeze has since been superseded and the adapter surface reopened for this tranche, and a new freeze boundary comes before any holdout re-run, so no result recorded under d9f75ef6 was taken with this capability in place.
